newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sues sports arena architect over disabled law.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sues sports arena architect over disabled law.

text.p: The Justice Department Thursday sued the nation's largest architectural firm for designing indoor sports arenas in six cities that fail to provide disabled spectators with an unobstructed view.

The lawsuit, filed in federal court in Minneapolis, charged that the firm, Ellerbe Beckett, designed arenas that do not comply with architectural standards for new facilities under the Americans with Disabilities Act.

Under the law, stadiums since 1993 must set aside at least one percent of their seating for wheelchair users, distribute them throughout the facility and provide lines of sight comparable to those of other spectators.

At issue in the case were professional basketball or hockey arenas recently built or being constructed in Boston, Buffalo, Cleveland, Philadelphia, Portland and Washington. The lawsuit seeks an order stopping the firm from continuing to design stadiums that do not provide a proper view for disabled spectators and a civil penalty.
Disability rights advocates in five of the cities already had filed similar private suits. The department's civil rights unit sued after eight months of settlement negotiations.
The Justice Department said organisers of the Summer Olympics in Atlanta agreed to provide wheelchair users with a line of sight over standing spectators at the Olympic Stadium and other sites.
